evidence: src/infrastructure/repositories/InMemoryProjectRepository.ts: InMemoryProjectRepository implements ProjectRepository and stores data in a private Map<string, Project>, with findById, findAll and save.

src/infrastructure/repositories/InMemoryTaskRepository.ts: InMemoryTaskRepository implements TaskRepository using a private Map<string, Task>. Its query methods findByProjectId, findByProjectIdAndStatus and findByProjectIdAndAssignee only filter stored data.
src/infrastructure/repositories/InMemoryUserRepository.ts: InMemoryUserRepository implements UserRepository and stores data in a private Map<string, User>, with findById, findAll and save.
All three classes use the same approach (`this.<map>.get(id) ?? null`, `this.<map>.set(entity.id, entity)`), so the abstraction is consistent and no domain abstraction is bypassed.
The only incoming dependency is src/infrastructure/app.ts, which composes the three repositories.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This module passes the rule. All three files deal with a single concern: in-memory storage behind the domain repository interfaces. Each class implements its matching domain interface and uses the same approach: a private Map keyed by entity id, a findById that returns null when nothing is found, and a save that writes to the Map. None of the files drift into business logic, call each other, or work around the domain abstractions. The findById/save code repeats across the three classes, but that is ordinary per-entity boilerplate, not a business rule or invariant copied in several places. In InMemoryTaskRepository, the projectId filter appears in three query methods. That is a minor implementation repetition that serves the TaskRepository interface, not a rule split across files.
